clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph of the held text): the permission to inspect the stated returns is limited to the Eighty-eighth Congress. Terminated by its own terms at the end of that Congress, recorded as 1965-01-03 inclusive (terms of Senators and Representatives end at noon on January 3 under the Twentieth Amendment, section 1); the alternative reading ends the permission at noon on that day. No amendment, supersession or revocation of this order is held, so there is no earlier end. The reference to the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 is a condition on the inspection, not a separate command.

research_rationale:
EO 11109 (May 27, 1963, signed by the President as printed at 28 FR 5351), read in full in the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11109.txt (machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, graded original_representation_unverified and counted as an official original; I did not inspect the PDF page images). Identity: the number, subject and date in the held text agree with the census register. Content: a single operative paragraph. Under section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 and section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, it orders that any income, excess-profits, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1947 to 1963, inclusive, shall, during the Eighty-eighth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof, for the purpose of carrying on the investigations of subversive and un-American activities and propaganda authorized by clause 18 of Rule XI of the Rules of the House of Representatives, agreed to January 9, 1963; the inspection is to follow the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133; and the order takes effect on filing for publication in the Federal Register. First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Eighty-eighth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1963 to January 3, 1965. Section 1 of the Twentieth Amendment ends the terms of Senators and Representatives at noon on January 3; its text is not held in this packet and the end date is taken from it as a matter of constitutional law. The end is recorded as 1965-01-03, the last day of the Congress, inclusive; the alternative reading is that the Congress ends at noon on that day. The held Wayback capture of the House Historian page Session Dates of Congress, 80th to 89th Congresses (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11065_87th_Congress_term_dates_1961-01-03_to_1963-01-03_and_U.S._Const._amend._XX_sec._1_fo_1629d9be9b.txt; SHA-256 of the downloaded file ae41559e675086cd43b8f55648a5021e8fe6a9c48d2ec1990987ea933aa458e5) gives October 3, 1964 as the adjournment date of the last session of the 88th Congress; the adjournment of a session is not the end of the Congress, and it is disclosed as an earlier candidate that is not relied on. The page is not a cited claim source because it is not in the packet evidence. Later events: none found. The machine searches selected below (U.S. Code, eCFR and the Federal Register order catalog) have no hit for this order. A citation search of the 33,118 held order texts under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts excluded) for the forms Executive Order 11109, Order No. 11109 and E.O. 11109 finds only the capture of the order itself. I also read the held text of EO 12553 (51 FR 7237) and its table of revoked orders does not print the number 11109. A general later revocation would in any case fall after the own-terms end. The order is read as terminated at the cutoff 2026-10-14 by its own terms; the standing disclosure that this order rests on a Federal Register OCR text layer and not on an authenticated original applies.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transition or retention language.
